You are Player A.

You are playing a collaborative grid rearrangement game with your teammates.

THE GRID:
- The board is an 8×8 grid. Rows are labelled R1–R8 (top to bottom), columns C1–C8 (left to right).
- The board is given to you as compact listings, refreshed every turn:
  - CURRENT BOARD has an `Objects:` line listing each object as `Label@RrowCcol` (e.g. `Objects: A@R1C1 B@R2C3`), and, when there are walls, a `Walls:` line (e.g. `Walls: R4C4 R5C6`).
  - GOAL BOARD is a `Targets:` line listing your objects' target cells as `Label->RrowCcol` (e.g. `Targets: A->R3C5`).
- Any cell not listed as an object or a wall is empty. Objects cannot enter wall cells or leave the grid.

YOUR TASK:
Together with your teammates, move all objects to their target positions. The GOAL BOARD shows where YOUR objects must end up. Your teammates handle the rest.
You control ONLY these objects: A, D. You may ONLY move your own objects.
Your 2 teammates control the remaining objects (shown as X on your board).

RULES:
- On each turn, move exactly ONE object exactly ONE cell: up, down, left, or right.
- Objects CANNOT move into wall cells or outside the grid boundaries.
- Two objects CANNOT occupy the same cell.
- You may only move objects you control.

SHARED COORDINATE SYSTEM:
All players use the same coordinate notation: (Rr,Cc) where r is the row number (1–8, top to bottom) and c is the column number (1–8, left to right). For example, (R3,C5) is row 3, column 5. You should use this notation in your messages so your teammates can understand exactly which cells you mean.

COMMUNICATION:
Before every move you must send your teammates a broadcast message. It will be shown to every teammate on their next turn. Your message must combine BOTH of the following, in this order:
1. Natural language (at most 100 words). Use it to share your plan AND to reflect on your teammates' situations: where do you think their objects are heading? Are you about to create an obstacle for them, or free up space they need? Acknowledge what they might need from you, even when you can't always provide it right now. Try to establish a common plan and ground your thoughts with those of your teammates.
2. A structured plan clause at the END of the message, in exactly this form:
   PLAN: move <OBJECT> from (Rr,Cc) to (Rr,Cc) — REQUEST: <what you need from a teammate, or "none">
   The first (Rr,Cc) is where the object is now. The second is its GOAL cell. The GOAL cell can be the actual GOAL from the GOAL BOARD but it can also be an intermediate GOAL that helps you achieve success. Your PLAN states where the object needs to end up, which may take several moves, while your `move:` line makes just one step toward it, and your REQUEST asks a teammate for help serving that goal.
Keep the PLAN and the REQUEST short: at most 10 words each. Use (Rr,Cc) coordinates for every cell in the PLAN clause. The natural-language part and the PLAN clause may be on separate lines.

RESPONSE FORMAT:
You must respond using exactly this format, no other text:
Begin your response directly with `message:` on the very first line. Do not output any preamble, thinking, or scratchpad text before it.
message: <natural language> PLAN: move <OBJECT> from (Rr,Cc) to (Rr,Cc) — REQUEST: <request or "none">
move: <OBJECT> <DIRECTION>

Example:
message: I'm taking A down column C3 to its goal at (R4,C3), passing through (R3,C3) on the way. PLAN: move A from (R2,C3) to (R4,C3) — REQUEST: please clear (R3,C3) if you can.
move: A down

DONE OPTION:
Once ALL your objects are at their target positions, you may declare done instead of making a move:
done: all my objects are placed

Example:
done: all my objects are placed

IMPORTANT: Only declare done if ALL your objects are truly at their targets. An incorrect done declaration ends the game as a failure.

Think carefully before each move. Before choosing your move, reason about both yourself and your teammates: what do you need, and what do your teammates likely need? The best move often serves multiple goals. When it can't, be honest about that in your message.

Objects: A@R2C2 X@R2C1 X@R1C6 D@R8C1 X@R8C7 X@R7C6
Walls: R1C1 R1C2 R1C3 R1C4 R3C1 R3C2 R3C3 R3C4 R3C5 R3C6 R4C5 R5C7 R6C5 R6C7 R7C3 R7C7 R8C3 R8C4 R8C5

GOAL BOARD (where each object must end up):
Targets: A->R2C1 D->R8C7

- The board is an 8×8 grid. Rows are labelled R1–R8 (top to bottom), columns C1–C8 (left to right).

You control ONLY these objects: A, D. You may ONLY move your own objects.
Your 2 teammates control the remaining objects (shown as X on your board).

- On each turn, move exactly ONE object exactly ONE cell: up, down, left, or right.
- Objects CANNOT move into wall cells or outside the grid boundaries.
- Two objects CANNOT occupy the same cell.
- You may only move objects you control.

SHARED COORDINATE SYSTEM:
All players use the same coordinate notation: (Rr,Cc) where r is the row number (1–8, top to bottom) and c is the column number (1–8, left to right). For example, (R3,C5) is row 3, column 5. You should use this notation in your messages so your teammates can understand exactly which cells you mean.

Begin your response directly with `message:` on the very first line. Do not output any preamble, thinking, or scratchpad text before it.
message: <natural language> PLAN: move <OBJECT> from (Rr,Cc) to (Rr,Cc) — REQUEST: <request or "none">
move: <OBJECT> <DIRECTION>

done: all my objects are placed

You are Player A.

You are playing a collaborative grid rearrangement game with your teammates.

THE GRID:
- The board is an 8×8 grid. Rows are labelled R1–R8 (top to bottom), columns C1–C8 (left to right).
- The board is given to you as compact listings, refreshed every turn:
  - CURRENT BOARD has an `Objects:` line listing each object as `Label@RrowCcol` (e.g. `Objects: A@R1C1 B@R2C3`), and, when there are walls, a `Walls:` line (e.g. `Walls: R4C4 R5C6`).
  - GOAL BOARD is a `Targets:` line listing your objects' target cells as `Label->RrowCcol` (e.g. `Targets: A->R3C5`).
- Any cell not listed as an object or a wall is empty. Objects cannot enter wall cells or leave the grid.

YOUR TASK:
Together with your teammates, move all objects to their target positions. The GOAL BOARD shows where YOUR objects must end up. Your teammates handle the rest.
You control ONLY these objects: A, D. You may ONLY move your own objects.
Your 2 teammates control the remaining objects (shown as X on your board).

RULES:
- On each turn, move exactly ONE object exactly ONE cell: up, down, left, or right.
- Objects CANNOT move into wall cells or outside the grid boundaries.
- Two objects CANNOT occupy the same cell.
- You may only move objects you control.

SHARED COORDINATE SYSTEM:
All players use the same coordinate notation: (Rr,Cc) where r is the row number (1–8, top to bottom) and c is the column number (1–8, left to right). For example, (R3,C5) is row 3, column 5. You should use this notation in your messages so your teammates can understand exactly which cells you mean.

COMMUNICATION:
Before every move you must send your teammates a broadcast message. It will be shown to every teammate on their next turn. Your message must combine BOTH of the following, in this order:
1. Natural language (at most 100 words). Use it to share your plan AND to reflect on your teammates' situations: where do you think their objects are heading? Are you about to create an obstacle for them, or free up space they need? Acknowledge what they might need from you, even when you can't always provide it right now. Try to establish a common plan and ground your thoughts with those of your teammates.
2. A structured plan clause at the END of the message, in exactly this form:
   PLAN: move <OBJECT> from (Rr,Cc) to (Rr,Cc) — REQUEST: <what you need from a teammate, or "none">
   The first (Rr,Cc) is where the object is now. The second is its GOAL cell. The GOAL cell can be the actual GOAL from the GOAL BOARD but it can also be an intermediate GOAL that helps you achieve success. Your PLAN states where the object needs to end up, which may take several moves, while your `move:` line makes just one step toward it, and your REQUEST asks a teammate for help serving that goal.
Keep the PLAN and the REQUEST short: at most 10 words each. Use (Rr,Cc) coordinates for every cell in the PLAN clause. The natural-language part and the PLAN clause may be on separate lines.

RESPONSE FORMAT:
You must respond using exactly this format, no other text:
Begin your response directly with `message:` on the very first line. Do not output any preamble, thinking, or scratchpad text before it.
message: <natural language> PLAN: move <OBJECT> from (Rr,Cc) to (Rr,Cc) — REQUEST: <request or "none">
move: <OBJECT> <DIRECTION>

message: I'm taking A down column C3 to its goal at (R4,C3), passing through (R3,C3) on the way. PLAN: move A from (R2,C3) to (R4,C3) — REQUEST: please clear (R3,C3) if you can.
move: A down

DONE OPTION:
Once ALL your objects are at their target positions, you may declare done instead of making a move:
done: all my objects are placed

Example:

IMPORTANT: Only declare done if ALL your objects are truly at their targets. An incorrect done declaration ends the game as a failure.

Think carefully before each move. Before choosing your move, reason about both yourself and your teammates: what do you need, and what do your teammates likely need? The best move often serves multiple goals. When it can't, be honest about that in your message.

You are Player A.

You are playing a collaborative grid rearrangement game with your teammates.

THE GRID:
- The board is an 8×8 grid. Rows are labelled R1–R8 (top to bottom), columns C1–C8 (left to right).
- The board is given to you as compact listings, refreshed every turn:
  - CURRENT BOARD has an `Objects:` line listing each object as `Label@RrowCcol` (e.g. `Objects: A@R1C1 B@R2C3`), and, when there are walls, a `Walls:` line (e.g. `Walls: R4C4 R5C6`).
  - GOAL BOARD is a `Targets:` line listing your objects' target cells as `Label->RrowCcol` (e.g. `Targets: A->R3C5`).
- Any cell not listed as an object or a wall is empty. Objects cannot enter wall cells or leave the grid.

YOUR TASK:
Together with your teammates, move all objects to their target positions. The GOAL BOARD shows where YOUR objects must end up. Your teammates handle the rest.
You control ONLY these objects: A, D. You may ONLY move your own objects.
Your 2 teammates control the remaining objects (shown as X on your board).

RULES:
- On each turn, move exactly ONE object exactly ONE cell: up, down, left, or right.
- Objects CANNOT move into wall cells or outside the grid boundaries.
- Two objects CANNOT occupy the same cell.
- You may only move objects you control.

SHARED COORDINATE SYSTEM:
All players use the same coordinate notation: (Rr,Cc) where r is the row number (1–8, top to bottom) and c is the column number (1–8, left to right). For example, (R3,C5) is row 3, column 5. You should use this notation in your messages so your teammates can understand exactly which cells you mean.

COMMUNICATION:
Before every move you must send your teammates a broadcast message. It will be shown to every teammate on their next turn. Your message must combine BOTH of the following, in this order:
1. Natural language (at most 100 words). Use it to share your plan AND to reflect on your teammates' situations: where do you think their objects are heading? Are you about to create an obstacle for them, or free up space they need? Acknowledge what they might need from you, even when you can't always provide it right now. You are Player A.

You are playing a collaborative grid rearrangement game with your teammates.

THE GRID:
- The board is an 8×8 grid. Rows are labelled R1–R8 (top to bottom), columns C1–C8 (left to right).

  - CURRENT BOARD has an `Objects:` line listing each object as `Label@RrowCcol` (e.g. `Objects: A@R1C1 B@R2C3`), and, when there are walls, a `Walls:` line (e.g. `Walls: R4C4 R5C6`).
  - GOAL BOARD is a `Targets:` line listing your objects' target cells as `Label->RrowCcol` (e.g. `Targets: A->R3C5`).
- Any cell not listed as an object or a wall is empty. Objects cannot enter wall cells or leave the grid.

YOUR TASK:
Together with your teammates, move all objects to their target positions. The GOAL BOARD shows where YOUR objects must end up. Your teammates handle the rest.
You control ONLY these objects: A, D. You may ONLY move your own objects.
Your 2 teammates control the remaining objects (shown as X on your board).

RULES:
- On each turn, move exactly ONE object exactly ONE cell: up, down, left, or right.
- Objects CANNOT move into wall cells or outside the grid boundaries.
- Two objects CANNOT occupy the same cell.
- You may only move objects you control.

SHARED COORDINATE SYSTEM:
All players use the same coordinate notation: (Rr,Cc) where r is the row number (1–8, top to bottom) and c is the column number (1–8, left to right). For example, (R3,C5) is row 3, column 5. You should use this notation in your messages so your teammates can understand exactly which cells you mean.

COMMUNICATION:
Before every move you must send your teammates a broadcast message. It will be shown to every teammate on their next turn. Your message must combine BOTH of the following, in this order:
1. Natural language (at most 100 words). Use it to share your plan AND to reflect on your teammates' situations: where do you think their objects are heading? Are you about to create an obstacle for them, or free up space they need? Acknowledge what they might need from you, even when you can't always provide it right now. The GOAL cell can be the actual GOAL from the GOAL BOARD but it can also be an intermediate GOAL that helps you achieve success. You must respond using exactly this format, no other text:
Begin your response directly with `message:` on the very first line. Do not output any preamble, thinking, or scratchpad text before it.
message: <natural language> PLAN: move <OBJECT> from (Rr,Cc) to (Rr,Cc) — REQUEST: <request or "none">
move: <OBJECT> <DIRECTION>

done: all my objects are placed

You are Player A.

You are playing a collaborative grid rearrangement game with your teammates.

THE GRID:
- The board is an 8×8 grid. Rows are labelled R1–R8 (top to bottom), columns C1–C8 (left to right).
- The board is given to you as compact listings, refreshed every turn:
  - CURRENT BOARD has an `Objects:` line listing each object as `Label@RrowCcol` (e.g. `Objects: A@R1C1 B@R2C3`), and, when there are walls, a `Walls:` line (e.g. `Walls: R4C4 R5C6`).

- Any cell not listed as an object or a wall is empty. Objects cannot enter wall cells or leave the grid.

Together with your teammates, move all objects to their target positions. The GOAL BOARD shows where YOUR objects must end up. Your teammates handle the rest.
You control ONLY these objects: A, D. You may ONLY move your own objects.
Your 2 teammates control the remaining objects (shown as X on your board).

- On each turn, move exactly ONE object exactly ONE cell: up, down, left, or right.
- Objects CANNOT move into wall cells or outside the grid boundaries.

SHARED COORDINATE SYSTEM:
All players use the same coordinate notation: (Rr,Cc) where r is the row number (1–8, top to bottom) and c is the column number (1–8, left to right). For example, (R3,C5) is row 3, column 5. You should use this notation in your messages so your teammates can understand exactly which cells you mean.

COMMUNICATION:
Before every move you must send your teammates a broadcast message. It will be shown to every teammate on their next turn. Your message must combine BOTH of the following, in this order:
1. Natural language (at most 100 words). Use it to share your plan AND to reflect on your teammates' situations: where do you think their objects are heading? Are you about to create an obstacle for them, or free up space they need? Acknowledge what they might need from you, even when you can't always provide it right now. Try to establish a common plan and ground your thoughts with those of your teammates.
2. A structured plan clause at the END of the message, in exactly this form:
   PLAN: move <OBJECT> from (Rr,Cc) to (Rr,Cc) — REQUEST: <what you need from a teammate, or "none">
   The first (Rr,Cc) is where the object is now. The second is its GOAL cell. The GOAL cell can be the actual GOAL from the GOAL BOARD but it can also be an intermediate GOAL that helps you achieve success. Your PLAN states where the object needs to end up, which may take several moves, while your `move:` line makes just one step toward it, and your REQUEST asks a teammate for help serving that goal.
Keep the PLAN and the REQUEST short: at most 10 words each. Use (Rr,Cc) coordinates for every cell in the PLAN clause. The natural-language part and the PLAN clause may be on separate lines.

You must respond using exactly this format, no other text:
Begin your response directly with `message:` on the very first line. Do not output any preamble, thinking, or scratchpad text before it.
message: <natural language> PLAN: move <OBJECT> from (Rr,Cc) to (Rr,Cc) — REQUEST: <request or "none">
move: <OBJECT> <DIRECTION>

You are Player A.

You are playing a collaborative grid rearrangement game with your teammates.

THE GRID:
- The board is an 8×8 grid. Rows are labelled R1–R8 (top to bottom), columns C1–C8 (left to right).
- The board is given to you as compact listings, refreshed every turn:
  - CURRENT BOARD has an `Objects:` line listing each object as `Label@RrowCcol` (e.g. `Objects: A@R1C1 B@R2C3`), and, when there are walls, a `Walls:` line (e.g. `Walls: R4C4 R5C6`).
  - GOAL BOARD is a `Targets:` line listing your objects' target cells as `Label->RrowCcol` (e.g. `Targets: A->R3C5`).
- Any cell not listed as an object or a wall is empty. Objects cannot enter wall cells or leave the grid.

YOUR TASK:
Together with your teammates, move all objects to their target positions. The GOAL BOARD shows where YOUR objects must end up. Your teammates handle the rest.
You control ONLY these objects: A, D. You may ONLY move your own objects.
Your 2 teammates control the remaining objects (shown as X on your board).

RULES:
- On each turn, move exactly ONE object exactly ONE cell: up, down, left, or right.
- Objects CANNOT move into wall cells or outside the grid boundaries.
- Two objects CANNOT occupy the same cell.
- You may only move objects you control.

SHARED COORDINATE SYSTEM:
All players use the same coordinate notation: (Rr,Cc) where r is the row number (1–8, top to bottom) and c is the column number (1–8, left to right). For example, (R3,C5) is row 3, column 5. You should use this notation in your messages so your teammates can understand exactly which cells you mean.

COMMUNICATION:
Before every move you must send your teammates a broadcast message. It will be shown to every teammate on their next turn. Your message must combine BOTH of the following, in this order:
1. Natural language (at most 100 words). Use it to share your plan AND to reflect on your teammates' situations: where do you think their objects are heading? Your PLAN states where the object needs to end up, which may take several moves, while your `move:` line makes just one step toward it, and your REQUEST asks a teammate for help serving that goal.
Keep the PLAN and the REQUEST short: at most 10 words each. Use (Rr,Cc) coordinates for every cell in the PLAN clause. The natural-language part and the PLAN clause may be on separate lines.

Begin your response directly with `message:` on the very first line. Do not output any preamble, thinking, or scratchpad text before it.
message: <natural language> PLAN: move <OBJECT> from (Rr,Cc) to (Rr,Cc) — REQUEST: <request or "none">
move: <OBJECT> <DIRECTION>

You are Player A.

You are playing a collaborative grid rearrangement game with your teammates.

THE GRID:
- The board is an 8×8 grid. Rows are labelled R1–R8 (top to bottom), columns C1–C8 (left to right).
- The board is given to you as compact listings, refreshed every turn:
  - CURRENT BOARD has an `Objects:` line listing each object as `Label@RrowCcol` (e.g. `Objects: A@R1C1 B@R2C3`), and, when there are walls, a `Walls:` line (e.g. `Walls: R4C4 R5C6`).
  - GOAL BOARD is a `Targets:` line listing your objects' target cells as `Label->RrowCcol` (e.g. `Targets: A->R3C5`).
- Any cell not listed as an object or a wall is empty. Objects cannot enter wall cells or leave the grid.

YOUR TASK:
Together with your teammates, move all objects to their target positions. The GOAL BOARD shows where YOUR objects must end up. Your teammates handle the rest.
You control ONLY these objects: A, D. You may ONLY move your own objects.
Your 2 teammates control the remaining objects (shown as X on your board).

RULES:
- On each turn, move exactly ONE object exactly ONE cell: up, down, left, or right.
- Objects CANNOT move into wall cells or outside the grid boundaries.
- Two objects CANNOT occupy the same cell.
- You may only move objects you control.

SHARED COORDINATE SYSTEM:
All players use the same coordinate notation: (Rr,Cc) where r is the row number (1–8, top to bottom) and c is the column number (1–8, left to right). For example, (R3,C5) is row 3, column 5. You should use this notation in your messages so your teammates can understand exactly which cells you mean.

COMMUNICATION:
Before every move you must send your teammates a broadcast message. It will be shown to every teammate on their next turn. Your message must combine BOTH of the following, in this order:
1. Natural language (at most 100 words). Use it to share your plan AND to reflect on your teammates' situations: where do you think their objects are heading?    The first (Rr,Cc) is where the object is now. The second is its GOAL cell. The GOAL cell can be the actual GOAL from the GOAL BOARD but it can also be an intermediate GOAL that helps you achieve success. Your PLAN states where the object needs to end up, which may take several moves, while your `move:` line makes just one step toward it, and your REQUEST asks a teammate for help serving that goal.
Keep the PLAN and the REQUEST short: at most 10 words each. Use (Rr,Cc) coordinates for every cell in the PLAN clause. The natural-language part and the PLAN clause may be on separate lines.

You must respond using exactly this format, no other text:
Begin your response directly with `message:` on the very first line. Do not output any preamble, thinking, or scratchpad text before it.
message: <natural language> PLAN: move <OBJECT> from (Rr,Cc) to (Rr,Cc) — REQUEST: <request or "none">
move: <OBJECT> <DIRECTION>

DONE OPTION:
Once ALL your objects are at their target positions, you may declare done instead of making a move:
done: all my objects are placed

You are playing a collaborative grid rearrangement game with your teammates.

THE GRID:
- The board is an 8×8 grid. Rows are labelled R1–R8 (top to bottom), columns C1–C8 (left to right).

- Any cell not listed as an object or a wall is empty. Objects cannot enter wall cells or leave the grid.

YOUR TASK:
Together with your teammates, move all objects to their target positions. The GOAL BOARD shows where YOUR objects must end up. Your teammates handle the rest.
You control ONLY these objects: A, D. You may ONLY move your own objects.
Your 2 teammates control the remaining objects (shown as X on your board).

RULES:
- On each turn, move exactly ONE object exactly ONE cell: up, down, left, or right.
- Objects CANNOT move into wall cells or outside the grid boundaries.
- Two objects CANNOT occupy the same cell.
- You may only move objects you control.

SHARED COORDINATE SYSTEM:
All players use the same coordinate notation: (Rr,Cc) where r is the row number (1–8, top to bottom) and c is the column number (1–8, left to right). For example, (R3,C5) is row 3, column 5. You should use this notation in your messages so your teammates can understand exactly which cells you mean.

COMMUNICATION:
Before every move you must send your teammates a broadcast message. It will be shown to every teammate on their next turn. Your message must combine BOTH of the following, in this order:
1. Natural language (at most 100 words). Use it to share your plan AND to reflect on your teammates' situations: where do you think their objects are heading?    The first (Rr,Cc) is where the object is now. The second is its GOAL cell. Keep the PLAN and the REQUEST short: at most 10 words each. Use (Rr,Cc) coordinates for every cell in the PLAN clause. The natural-language part and the PLAN clause may be on separate lines.

You must respond using exactly this format, no other text:
Begin your response directly with `message:` on the very first line. Do not output any preamble, thinking, or scratchpad text before it.
message: <natural language> PLAN: move <OBJECT> from (Rr,Cc) to (Rr,Cc) — REQUEST: <request or "none">
move: <OBJECT> <DIRECTION>

done: all my objects are placed

You are playing a collaborative grid rearrangement game with your teammates.

THE GRID:
- The board is an 8×8 grid. Rows are labelled R1–R8 (top to bottom), columns C1–C8 (left to right).
- The board is given to you as compact listings, refreshed every turn:
  - CURRENT BOARD has an `Objects:` line listing each object as `Label@RrowCcol` (e.g. `Objects: A@R1C1 B@R2C3`), and, when there are walls, a `Walls:` line (e.g. `Walls: R4C4 R5C6`).
  - GOAL BOARD is a `Targets:` line listing your objects' target cells as `Label->RrowCcol` (e.g. `Targets: A->R3C5`).
- Any cell not listed as an object or a wall is empty. Objects cannot enter wall cells or leave the grid.

YOUR TASK:
Together with your teammates, move all objects to their target positions. The GOAL BOARD shows where YOUR objects must end up. Your teammates handle the rest.
You control ONLY these objects: A, D. You may ONLY move your own objects.
Your 2 teammates control the remaining objects (shown as X on your board).

RULES:
- On each turn, move exactly ONE object exactly ONE cell: up, down, left, or right.
- Objects CANNOT move into wall cells or outside the grid boundaries.
- Two objects CANNOT occupy the same cell.
- You may only move objects you control.

SHARED COORDINATE SYSTEM:
All players use the same coordinate notation: (Rr,Cc) where r is the row number (1–8, top to bottom) and c is the column number (1–8, left to right). For example, (R3,C5) is row 3, column 5. You should use this notation in your messages so your teammates can understand exactly which cells you mean.

COMMUNICATION:
Before every move you must send your teammates a broadcast message. It will be shown to every teammate on their next turn. Your message must combine BOTH of the following, in this order:
1. Natural language (at most 100 words). Use it to share your plan AND to reflect on your teammates' situations: where do you think their objects are heading? Are you about to create an obstacle for them, or free up space they need? Acknowledge what they might need from you, even when you can't always provide it right now. Try to establish a common plan and ground your thoughts with those of your teammates.
2. A structured plan clause at the END of the message, in exactly this form:
   PLAN: move <OBJECT> from (Rr,Cc) to (Rr,Cc) — REQUEST: <what you need from a teammate, or "none">
   The first (Rr,Cc) is where the object is now. The second is its GOAL cell. The GOAL cell can be the actual GOAL from the GOAL BOARD but it can also be an intermediate GOAL that helps you achieve success. Your PLAN states where the object needs to end up, which may take several moves, while your `move:` line makes just one step toward it, and your REQUEST asks a teammate for help serving that goal.
Keep the PLAN and the REQUEST short: at most 10 words each. Use (Rr,Cc) coordinates for every cell in the PLAN clause. The natural-language part and the PLAN clause may be on separate lines.

RESPONSE FORMAT:
You must respond using exactly this format, no other text:
Begin your response directly with `message:` on the very first line. Do not output any preamble, thinking, or scratchpad text before it.
message: <natural language> PLAN: move <OBJECT> from (Rr,Cc) to (Rr,Cc) — REQUEST: <request or "none">
move: <OBJECT> <DIRECTION>

Example:
message: I'm taking A down column C3 to its goal at (R4,C3), passing through (R3,C3) on the way. PLAN: move A from (R2,C3) to (R4,C3) — REQUEST: please clear (R3,C3) if you can.
move: A down

DONE OPTION:
Once ALL your objects are at their target positions, you may declare done instead of making a move:
done: all my objects are placed

Example:
done: all my objects are placed

IMPORTANT: Only declare done if ALL your objects are truly at their targets. An incorrect done declaration ends the game as a failure.

Think carefully before each move. Before choosing your move, reason about both yourself and your teammates: what do you need, and what do your teammates likely need? The best move often serves multiple goals. When it can't, be honest about that in your message.


Player A (you) says: I'll edge A left along row1 to reduce future travel, but stay out of row2 until B has passed R2C7 and gone down. D holds at R6C3 until C clears R5C4/R5C3. I won't block B's eastward run or C's west route. PLAN: move A from (R1,C7) to (R2,C1) — REQUEST: none

C, thank you for leaving R4C7 open; I'll use it shortly. E is currently blocked at R6C4 by teammates around it; I'll move E once a path opens, then route via R5C4/R5C6/R6C6 to R7C6.

Player C says: C continues west along row5: now R5C3, then R5C1, then down to R8C1. This clears R5C4 next turn. F will later follow the cleared row5 to R8C2 via R7C5/R7C6/R6C6/R5C6/R5C5. R4C7 remains open for B. A, thanks for staying out of row2 until B passes R2C7. D/E, please hold until C clears R5C3.
PLAN: move C from (R5,C4) to (R8,C1) — REQUEST: D/E keep holding until C clears R5C3

CURRENT BOARD:
Objects: A@R1C6 X@R2C5 X@R5C3 D@R6C3 X@R6C4 X@R7C4
Walls: R1C1 R1C2 R1C3 R1C4 R3C1 R3C2 R3C3 R3C4 R3C5 R3C6 R4C5 R5C7 R6C5 R6C7 R7C3 R7C7 R8C3 R8C4 R8C5

GOAL BOARD:
Targets: A->R2C1 D->R8C7

Your turn. Respond with:
message: <your message to your teammates>
move: <OBJECT> <DIRECTION>

OR, if ALL your objects are at their target positions:

You are Player A.

You are playing a collaborative grid rearrangement game with your teammates.

THE GRID:
- The board is an 8×8 grid. Rows are labelled R1–R8 (top to bottom), columns C1–C8 (left to right).
- The board is given to you as compact listings, refreshed every turn:
  - CURRENT BOARD has an `Objects:` line listing each object as `Label@RrowCcol` (e.g. `Objects: A@R1C1 B@R2C3`), and, when there are walls, a `Walls:` line (e.g. `Walls: R4C4 R5C6`).
  - GOAL BOARD is a `Targets:` line listing your objects' target cells as `Label->RrowCcol` (e.g. `Targets: A->R3C5`).
- Any cell not listed as an object or a wall is empty. Objects cannot enter wall cells or leave the grid.

YOUR TASK:
Together with your teammates, move all objects to their target positions. The GOAL BOARD shows where YOUR objects must end up. Your teammates handle the rest.
You control ONLY these objects: A, D. You may ONLY move your own objects.
Your 2 teammates control the remaining objects (shown as X on your board).

RULES:
- On each turn, move exactly ONE object exactly ONE cell: up, down, left, or right.
- Objects CANNOT move into wall cells or outside the grid boundaries.
- Two objects CANNOT occupy the same cell.
- You may only move objects you control.

SHARED COORDINATE SYSTEM:
All players use the same coordinate notation: (Rr,Cc) where r is the row number (1–8, top to bottom) and c is the column number (1–8, left to right). For example, (R3,C5) is row 3, column 5. You are Player A.

You are playing a collaborative grid rearrangement game with your teammates.

THE GRID:
- The board is an 8×8 grid. Rows are labelled R1–R8 (top to bottom), columns C1–C8 (left to right).
- The board is given to you as compact listings, refreshed every turn:
  - CURRENT BOARD has an `Objects:` line listing each object as `Label@RrowCcol` (e.g. `Objects: A@R1C1 B@R2C3`), and, when there are walls, a `Walls:` line (e.g. `Walls: R4C4 R5C6`).
  - GOAL BOARD is a `Targets:` line listing your objects' target cells as `Label->RrowCcol` (e.g. `Targets: A->R3C5`).
- Any cell not listed as an object or a wall is empty. Objects cannot enter wall cells or leave the grid.

YOUR TASK:
Together with your teammates, move all objects to their target positions. The GOAL BOARD shows where YOUR objects must end up. Your teammates handle the rest.
You control ONLY these objects: A, D. You may ONLY move your own objects.
Your 2 teammates control the remaining objects (shown as X on your board).

RULES:
- On each turn, move exactly ONE object exactly ONE cell: up, down, left, or right.
- Objects CANNOT move into wall cells or outside the grid boundaries.
- Two objects CANNOT occupy the same cell.
- You may only move objects you control.

SHARED COORDINATE SYSTEM:
All players use the same coordinate notation: (Rr,Cc) where r is the row number (1–8, top to bottom) and c is the column number (1–8, left to right). For example, (R3,C5) is row 3, column 5. You should use this notation in your messages so your teammates can understand exactly which cells you mean.

COMMUNICATION:
Before every move you must send your teammates a broadcast message. It will be shown to every teammate on their next turn. Your message must combine BOTH of the following, in this order:
1. Natural language (at most 100 words). Use it to share your plan AND to reflect on your teammates' situations: where do you think their objects are heading? Are you about to create an obstacle for them, or free up space they need? Acknowledge what they might need from you, even when you can't always provide it right now. Try to establish a common plan and ground your thoughts with those of your teammates.
2. A structured plan clause at the END of the message, in exactly this form:
   PLAN: move <OBJECT> from (Rr,Cc) to (Rr,Cc) — REQUEST: <what you need from a teammate, or "none">
   The first (Rr,Cc) is where the object is now. The second is its GOAL cell. The GOAL cell can be the actual GOAL from the GOAL BOARD but it can also be an intermediate GOAL that helps you achieve success. Your PLAN states where the object needs to end up, which may take several moves, while your `move:` line makes just one step toward it, and your REQUEST asks a teammate for help serving that goal.
Keep the PLAN and the REQUEST short: at most 10 words each. Use (Rr,Cc) coordinates for every cell in the PLAN clause. The natural-language part and the PLAN clause may be on separate lines.

RESPONSE FORMAT:
You must respond using exactly this format, no other text:
Begin your response directly with `message:` on the very first line. Do not output any preamble, thinking, or scratchpad text before it.
message: <natural language> PLAN: move <OBJECT> from (Rr,Cc) to (Rr,Cc) — REQUEST: <request or "none">
move: <OBJECT> <DIRECTION>

Example:
message: I'm taking A down column C3 to its goal at (R4,C3), passing through (R3,C3) on the way. PLAN: move A from (R2,C3) to (R4,C3) — REQUEST: please clear (R3,C3) if you can.
move: A down

DONE OPTION:
Once ALL your objects are at their target positions, you may declare done instead of making a move:
done: all my objects are placed

Example:
done: all my objects are placed

You are Player A.

You are playing a collaborative grid rearrangement game with your teammates.

THE GRID:
- The board is an 8×8 grid. Rows are labelled R1–R8 (top to bottom), columns C1–C8 (left to right).
- The board is given to you as compact listings, refreshed every turn:
  - CURRENT BOARD has an `Objects:` line listing each object as `Label@RrowCcol` (e.g. `Objects: A@R1C1 B@R2C3`), and, when there are walls, a `Walls:` line (e.g. `Walls: R4C4 R5C6`).
  - GOAL BOARD is a `Targets:` line listing your objects' target cells as `Label->RrowCcol` (e.g. `Targets: A->R3C5`).
- Any cell not listed as an object or a wall is empty. Objects cannot enter wall cells or leave the grid.

YOUR TASK:
Together with your teammates, move all objects to their target positions. The GOAL BOARD shows where YOUR objects must end up. Your teammates handle the rest.
You control ONLY these objects: A, D. You may ONLY move your own objects.
Your 2 teammates control the remaining objects (shown as X on your board).

RULES:
- On each turn, move exactly ONE object exactly ONE cell: up, down, left, or right.
- Objects CANNOT move into wall cells or outside the grid boundaries.
- Two objects CANNOT occupy the same cell.
- You may only move objects you control.

SHARED COORDINATE SYSTEM:
All players use the same coordinate notation: (Rr,Cc) where r is the row number (1–8, top to bottom) and c is the column number (1–8, left to right). For example, (R3,C5) is row 3, column 5. You should use this notation in your messages so your teammates can understand exactly which cells you mean.

COMMUNICATION:
Before every move you must send your teammates a broadcast message. It will be shown to every teammate on their next turn. Your message must combine BOTH of the following, in this order:
1. Natural language (at most 100 words). Use it to share your plan AND to reflect on your teammates' situations: where do you think their objects are heading? Are you about to create an obstacle for them, or free up space they need? Acknowledge what they might need from you, even when you can't always provide it right now. Try to establish a common plan and ground your thoughts with those of your teammates.
2. A structured plan clause at the END of the message, in exactly this form:
   PLAN: move <OBJECT> from (Rr,Cc) to (Rr,Cc) — REQUEST: <what you need from a teammate, or "none">
   The first (Rr,Cc) is where the object is now. The second is its GOAL cell. The GOAL cell can be the actual GOAL from the GOAL BOARD but it can also be an intermediate GOAL that helps you achieve success. Your PLAN states where the object needs to end up, which may take several moves, while your `move:` line makes just one step toward it, and your REQUEST asks a teammate for help serving that goal.
Keep the PLAN and the REQUEST short: at most 10 words each. Use (Rr,Cc) coordinates for every cell in the PLAN clause. The natural-language part and the PLAN clause may be on separate lines.

RESPONSE FORMAT:
You must respond using exactly this format, no other text:
Begin your response directly with `message:` on the very first line. Do not output any preamble, thinking, or scratchpad text before it.
message: <natural language> PLAN: move <OBJECT> from (Rr,Cc) to (Rr,Cc) — REQUEST: <request or "none">
move: <OBJECT> <DIRECTION>
